correctness.rationale: A published complete classification theorem lists seven pairwise non-isomorphic two-dimensional complex associative algebras. The 2023 quasi-centroid theorem has only five rows. Direct solution of the defining equations gives dimensions 4,3,3,1,1,2,2 for the seven classes. The two classes absent from the five-row profile are the zero algebra, whose quasi-centroid is all of End(C^2), and the algebra with sole product e1*e1=e1, whose quasi-centroid is the full lower-triangular matrix algebra. The packaged exact checker reconstructs every linear system and verifies the displayed bases.

value.rationale: The claim repairs an exhaustiveness statement in the smallest nontrivial dimension and supplies the full corrected table rather than a single counterexample. The omission changes the attainable quasi-centroid dimensions by introducing dimension 4 and duplicates the dimension-3 stratum with a structurally different decomposable algebra. Because the paper uses low-dimensional tables as classification data for quasi-centroids and quasi-derivations, a complete base case is mathematically useful for comparison and downstream low-dimensional structure calculations.
